key_insight: MCL-PINNs is a specialized phase-field neural solver that combines physics-informed learning with time-marching and adaptive training tricks to handle moving contact line problems with dynamic boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free way to simulate wetting, droplet motion, and interfacial evolution more robustly in complex fluid systems where sharp interfaces and contact-line dynamics are difficult for standard PINNs.
method: Discrete-time phase-field solver with a multi-network time-marching scheme
Relaxed output distribution constraints plus variable scaling for sharp interfacial features
Adaptive loss weighting and adaptive collocation sampling with interface extraction; symmetry-aware inputs when applicable
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on three benchmark scenarios—droplet coalescence, shear-induced droplet deformation, and dynamic wetting in a heterogeneous channel—showing improved accuracy and robustness over standard PINN formulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful loss balancing, adaptive sampling, and problem-specific scaling, so implementation complexity may limit ease of use and transferability.
paper_title: A phase-field neural solver for moving contact line problems with dynamic boundary conditions
